title: The ordinary coefficient restriction tensor pullback square
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, let $R,S$ be commutative ring sheaves on their small pro-etale sites and let $c:f^{-1}R\simeq S$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Write $A=f^{-1}R$, $C=f^*_c$, $I=f^*_{\mathrm{id}_A}$ and $U=\operatorname{Res}_c$. Let $\beta:CU\simeq I$ be the canonical ordinary pullback comparison with identity base restriction removed [lem-pbc-coefficient-pullback-factorization]. For any RingIsoTensorTransport $o$ for $c$ [lem-sfb-ring-isomorphism-tensor-transport], write $\delta:U(M\otimes_S N)\to UM\otimes_A UN$ for its normalized ordinary tensor map. Let $\mu_c$ and $\mu_i$ be the canonical ordinary tensor pullback isomorphisms [def-sp-proetale-ordinary-tensor-pullback-total]. For every two $R$-module sheaves $M,N$, one has $U(\mu_c(M,N)^{-1});\beta_{M\otimes_R N}=\delta_{CM,CN};(\beta_M\otimes_A\beta_N);\mu_i(M,N)^{-1}$. This is an equality of ordinary module-sheaf morphisms, with no complexes, totalization, localization or flatness assumptions.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, universal bilinear-map proof; compatibility of the two coefficient coordinates.

proof.text: Apply the unit identity for the adjunction-mate correspondence to the existing ordinary restriction/pullback mate. Its right mate is the coefficient direct-image comparison, which is identity on every section. After removing base identity restriction, the inverse of ordinaryPullback therefore sends the identity-coefficient pullback unit of every section to its c-coefficient pullback unit. This is the private lemma ordinaryPullback_inv_unit.

Transpose the inverse-oriented ordinary module tensor square under the identity-coefficient module adjunction. Test the two resulting maps on pure tensors using the sheafification adjunction and the presheaf tensor universal property. The preceding unit formula, both ordinary tensor comparison unit normalizations, and o.pure_hom give the same tensor of c-coefficient pullback unit sections. Tensor naturality on pure sections completes ordinary_inverse_square. Invert the isomorphisms to obtain ordinary_square, with the orientation required by the total comparison.

Compose the inverse-oriented equality with the coefficient and tensor isomorphisms and cancel their inverse pairs. TensorIso supplies the inverse of the tensor of the coefficient components. This gives the displayed orientation without changing any normalization.

proof_origin.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback: adjunction and bilinear-map universal property.

theorem ordinary_square
    (o : SheafOfModules.RingIsoTensorTransport
      (J := ProEt.topology X)
      (R := (proEtaleSheafInverseImage f CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj R) (S := S) c)
    (M N : proEtaleRingModules Y R) :
    (pbcRestrict c.hom).map (proEtaleOrdinaryTensorPullback f R S c M N).inv ≫
        (ordinaryPullback f R S c).hom.app
          (((proEtaleOrdinaryTensor Y R).obj M).obj N) =
      o.monoidal.toMonoidal.toOplaxMonoidal.δ
          ((proEtaleRingModulePullback f R S c).obj M)
          ((proEtaleRingModulePullback f R S c).obj N) ≫
        (SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory
          ((proEtaleSheafInverseImage f CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj R)).tensorHom
          ((ordinaryPullback f R S c).hom.app M)
          ((ordinaryPullback f R S c).hom.app N) ≫
        (proEtaleOrdinaryTensorPullback f R
          ((proEtaleSheafInverseImage f CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj R)
          (Iso.refl _) M N).inv
